parts.text: Compare SQLite and Postgres for the per-machine ledger. Which should we use and why? No code changes.
I'll check what the ledger stores and how it syncs.
The ledger is one file per machine, written offline, synced in batches.
SQLite in WAL mode allows one writer at a time with many readers.

Use SQLite for the per-machine ledger. It needs no server, works offline, and one writer at a time is enough because a single collector process writes it. Postgres stays the central store. Open question: how large a ledger gets before pruning is needed.

reference.request: Compare SQLite and Postgres for the per-machine ledger and recommend one, without changing code.
reference.done: Read docs/ledger.md and searched SQLite write limits. Recommended SQLite for the per-machine ledger: no server, works offline, and one writer at a time is enough because a single collector writes it. Postgres remains the central store.
reference.learned: SQLite in WAL mode allows one writer and many readers, which fits a single-collector ledger.
reference.open_items: Decide how large a ledger may grow before pruning.

facts.subject: per-machine ledger
facts.claim: The per-machine ledger should be SQLite because it needs no server and works offline.
